authoring.readiness: Proposed for 12–35 months, pending independent review. The child has voluntarily drawn attention to something, through any familiar communication method. The adult can join without moving the child or handling the surroundings.
authoring.exclusions: No collecting, carrying, reaching, climbing, window approach or new objects. Do not use this invitation during travel, road crossing, cooking, feeding or other attention-critical care. Uncertain communication/access needs require review.
authoring.changesFromDraft: Removed invented birds, colours and scenery. Restricted the draft to an existing indoor position; eliminated the window/outdoor variant. Added a concrete response to ambiguity and explicit stop/context boundaries.

template.title: Notice it together
template.summary: Stay with something your child has already noticed in the room.
template.instructions: When your child draws your attention to something in the familiar room, acknowledge it from where you already are. If you know what they mean, offer a short comment about that actual thing. If you are unsure, say so and leave space. Follow their next contribution, or finish when their attention moves on. Do not fetch or move anything.
template.conversation_prompt: “I’m looking too.” If you are not sure what they mean: “I’m not sure which thing you mean.” No answer is required.
template.look_for: An optional note might name what your child indicated and your response. Do not turn a glance into a claim about a lasting interest.
template.why_it_matters: The adult practises sharing attention without taking over. Responsive-care guidance is the general basis; this exact setting and script have not been evaluated.
template.safety_note: Keep ordinary care and safety first. This invitation adds no objects, touch or repositioning. Stay attentive throughout, use only the familiar setting described and stop whenever care is needed. Existing individual professional guidance takes priority.
template.parent_preparation: Use a familiar indoor place where neither of you needs to move or reach to join in. This is not a window, balcony or outdoor activity. The two-minute estimate is only for planning.
template.adult_role: Acknowledge what actually caught their attention. Avoid adding a guessing game or a stream of questions.
template.child_choices: They can point, use words or another familiar communication method, disagree with your interpretation, move on or decline company.
template.make_easier: Acknowledge their invitation without naming or explaining the object.
template.extend_activity: If they add something, respond to that detail. Keep the same place and materials; do not set a search task.
template.stop_signals: Stop if they turn away, decline, become uncomfortable or need care. Stop rather than moving closer to something unsafe or inaccessible.
template.avoid_prompt: Do not invent a bird, colour or event. Do not ask them to identify an object correctly, make eye contact or stay until a timer ends.
template.source_note: Original MIRA draft, not a reproduction or endorsement by a source organisation. Linked claims concern general practice or programmes, not this activity's efficacy. The proposed ages, timing, requirements and variations need independent exact-version review.
